The first is the `Changelog:` line that, since the add-changelog change of 2026-10-14, openspec/config.yaml requires at the end of every proposal and that archiving copies into CHANGELOG.md. In practice it appears in only 5 of the 175 archived proposals, and in 5 of the 10 archived since the rule. The second is a status change when work lands. Our v2 spec still reads "awaiting spec review" although 0.2.0 was tagged on 2026-10-15.
kept.recommendation: keep ours: one design spec per release stays. Adopt two pieces: every experiment-proposal spec ends with a `Changelog: <sentence>` line that is copied into the governance-7 CHANGELOG at release, and the spec's Status line gains `landed <tag>` when the release is tagged. Apply both to v3 itself and back-fill v2.

kept.title: Nothing tells us when a project we vendor publishes a new release; upstream automates the same check for its own pins
kept.claim: Upstream runs two weekly workflows that compare its pinned tools with what is published: the OpenSpec CLI against npm, and its model list against OpenRouter's catalog. Each opens a bump PR that a person merges. Those pins are tools, not vendored source code, so the check is analogous rather than the same. The vault already runs one such check, the weekly `okf-spec-drift` job in quality.yml, but none for the plugin's three vendored pins (a38b7b1, 98c7fae, f93fee7). The v3 spec plans none either. A `git ls-remote` check today would show three different results. hutzelmann/thesis-proposal-skills is behind: HEAD is 1666e69 (v0.9.0), and our pin is untagged, at v0.8.0-42. K-Dense-AI/scientific-agents has no tags, and its HEAD equals our pin 98c7fae. mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills now returns "Repository not found". The governance-1 arXiv HTTPS/XML fix in upstream v0.9.0 came to light only through this manual comparison. Recommendation (small cost): either add the three pins to the existing scheduled drift-job pattern, or write a live_net test run at each plugin release. The test compares `git ls-remote <url> HEAD` with each pinned SHA and reports an unreachable upstream as its own finding, since a `--tags` comparison would find nothing on K-Dense and fail on pm-claude-skills.
kept.recommendation: adopt a small version: one test under the suite's live_net marker that runs `git ls-remote --tags` against each vendored upstream and fails when a release tag newer than the recorded one exists. Run it at each plugin release, not weekly.

kept.title: Release and tagging: their main holds only released states; our main gained two untagged commits after 0.2.0
kept.claim: Upstream cuts a release with one local command, `poe release`, which runs `scripts/changelog.py release`. It writes the CHANGELOG section, sets pyproject.toml and uv.lock, stamps every SKILL.md, commits and makes an annotated `vX.Y.Z` tag on that commit. It fast-forwards `main` only when the release is cut on `develop`; `release_branch()` lets `main` cut a release itself before `develop` exists, which was the 0.9.0 transition. The command never pushes, and the pre-push hook refuses any push from a shell with no terminal. AGENTS.md:20 says main 'holds released versions only', but that rule dates from 0.9.0 (2026-10-15): 0.5.0-0.8.0 were tagged retroactively on 2026-10-14. In 0.9.0, two commits (4dfee0a, 1666e69) landed after the stamp commit 67dedad and the v0.9.0 tag sits on 1666e69, so the tag was placed by hand afterwards. What holds is that main's HEAD is currently tagged. The local clone fetched only main, so `develop` cannot be checked here. stamp_version.py itself says commits after a stamp 'ship with the older version still inside: the stamp is a floor'. On our side, we make an annotated `experiment-proposal--v<version>` tag after the branch lands on main with `--ff-only`, and plugin.json is the only place the version is written. Since the 0.2.0 tag, main has gained two untagged commits. Only 13035fb touches what users get: it copies plugin.json's description into the marketplace entry, a sync toward the single version source rather than drift away from it, and users receive it with no version change. de74cfe touches only docs/research. The comparison should not say that upstream stamps each SKILL.md because its marketplace entry has no version, or that our single writer prevents the drift. Our marketplace entry has no version either. Upstream has no plugin.json at all: the version lives in pyproject.toml and is stamped into the skills, because install.py and `npx skills add` deliver bare skill folders and `poe identify` reads the stamp to resolve bug reports. Our plugin.json does the same job inside the delivered folder, and like their stamp it does not stop untagged commits after a release from shipping. Our marketplace also lists a second plugin, research-vault, with source "./", so every main commit already reaches that plugin's users, and a 'main holds released states only' rule cannot work in this shared repo. Recommendation unchanged: keep the single writer and the `--ff-only` landing, with no develop branch and no pre-push hook. Once the governance-7 changelog exists, add one rule: any commit after a tag that changes plugins/experiment-proposal/ or its marketplace entry goes under [Unreleased] and ships in the next patch tag. The cost is small, assuming governance-7 lands.
kept.recommendation: keep ours: the single version writer, plus the release branch merged into main with --ff-only. No develop branch and no pre-push hook. Adopt one rule through the governance-7 changelog: any commit after a tag that changes plugins/experiment-proposal/ or its marketplace entry goes under [Unreleased] and ships in the next patch tag.

kept.title: v3 supersedes v2 but does not give v2 a Disposition line, as v2 did for the first spec
kept.claim: The gap is real. v2 superseded the first spec only partly, and its Bookkeeping bullet still gave the first spec a `Disposition: superseded-by:` header. v3 also supersedes v2 only partly ("where it changes it"), but has no bookkeeping step. v2 will therefore carry no pointer to v3, though v3 replaces v2's invocation decision (v2:17, `disable-model-invocation: true`) and its vendored-text rule (v2:89 and the v2:151 non-goal, which v3 breaks with a body edit to the-ethics-board). v2 also stays inside `_active_design_specs()`, so the repo keeps checking it as a current-state surface. No repo-wide convention requires the pointer; v2 set the precedent itself. The fix is one bookkeeping bullet in v3 plus one header line in v2, which the existing Disposition-value test already accepts. Upstream is not an equivalent. OpenSpec avoids the problem by design: archived change folders (`openspec/changes/archive/<date>-<id>/`) record deltas, and the current state lives in a separate canonical `openspec/specs/` tree. Upstream has no supersession pointer at all.
kept.recommendation: adopt: add a bookkeeping bullet to v3 section 4: v2 gets `Disposition: superseded-by: 2026-10-23-experiment-proposal-v3-design.md (<date>; every decision v3 does not name stands)` under its title. The repo's existing check on Disposition values then covers it.

kept.title: Their CHANGELOG records every change since the pin to the files we vendored, so the re-vendor review can start from it
kept.claim: Every change since a38b7b1 to the nine vendored scripts has a 0.9.0 CHANGELOG entry. a721bfd is classify-arxiv-answers (Fixed and Security), b311e4f is utf8-script-output (Fixed) and b5d24b5 is tighten-proposal-family (Changed: output sizing, default 5 instead of 20). crossref.py, dblp.py, openalex.py, opencitations.py and semantic_scholar.py are unchanged. Nothing that touches the vendored files is pending upstream: [Unreleased] is empty, and the remote's develop and main both point at v0.9.0 (1666e69). The local clone has no develop branch, so this was checked with `git ls-remote`. The two open bump PRs touch only harness/models.toml and scripts/validate_specs.py. The pin a38b7b1 sits between v0.8.0 and v0.9.0 and is not a tag, so the 0.9.0 section also holds entries from before the pin (for example sharpen-swap-test-anchors, which is a38b7b1 itself). A re-vendor review should start from the release section that contains the old pin and keep only the entries whose commits come after it, rather than reading 'sections between the old and new tags'.
kept.recommendation: no action beyond governance-2. At each future re-vendor, read the CHANGELOG sections between the old and new tags and list their archive links in the re-vendor commit message.

kept.title: The six substance tests we restate have not changed upstream since the pin
kept.claim: Upstream's six substance tests (shared/guidelines/guidelines.md and its per-skill references/ copies) have not changed since a38b7b1. Our checklist items 13.6 to 13.11 restate all six, and 13.8 includes the named-tool/domain clause the pin commit added, adapted to "device, system or domain". So our restatement matches the current one-line test definitions. It does not carry the longer paragraph from the same commit (guidelines.md:127) on how a name can pass: object of study, constraint source, unique data or access, an argued case, plus the title-blocker and Bachelor's rules. That gap is a separate question from upstream drift.
kept.recommendation: no action.

kept.title: Licence: our notices meet their MIT condition, and they ask for no citation
kept.claim: Their LICENSE.txt has one condition: the copyright notice and permission notice must accompany copies. plugins/experiment-proposal/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md ships in the folder the marketplace installs and reproduces their copyright line and the full permission text, and each of the nine vendored scripts names the copyright holder and MIT in its header. LICENSE.txt is unchanged between pin a38b7b1 and HEAD, so a re-vendor keeps the same copyright line. They have no CITATION.cff, and their README only asks people to open an issue before a PR, so our README is right to list only K-Dense and pm-claude-skills as asking to be cited. The six substance tests (checklist 13.6-13.11) are a close paraphrase rather than a clean restatement: several clauses match their guidelines.md word for word. The licence condition is still met, because the Hutzelmann notice already ships in the same folder, but ATTRIBUTION.md ("no text reproduced") and checklist.md ("in our own words") should say "adapted, with some wording kept". At the re-vendor, update the sha in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, ATTRIBUTION.md and the nine script headers. The notices file has no tag to update.
kept.recommendation: no action. At the re-vendor, change only the sha and tag in the notices.

refuted.title: No criterion for a permission, licence or data access the hypotheses depend on
refuted.reason: The upstream quotes are accurate (guidelines.md lines 147 and 153), but the evidence about our side does not hold. `grep -n 'CARE permission'` matches lines 29, 600 and 612, not only line 29. Line 600 says "CARE permission needed by 2 November, else the pilot runs without CARE". The finding quotes line 115 only up to "the CARE measure [18]", and the same sentence goes on to say "it awaits Prof. Mercer's permission (Appendix E.1): without it by 2 November the pilot runs without CARE, and if refused, PETS [26] replaces it". E.1 (line 433) and E.9 (line 519) state the same fallback. In git history, the fallback was in the draft at every review commit (0ce404d, 8741fc7, 65073d8, 440c9e5): first as [FALLBACK EMPATHY SCALE], later as PETS. At each of those commits, review.md item 2.5 records "CARE permission (Design) ... each have a response". So our checklist item 2.5 ("Each expected challenge ... has a planned response stated in the section it affects") is the matching criterion, and it did check this dependency. The 0 hits for 'licen|permission' come from searching for keywords, not for the function. A narrower gap remains: upstream also requires that the fallback keeps every research question answerable as asked, and treats an indispensable resource whose availability is in doubt as a blocker. Our 2.5 asks only for a planned response. That is a different claim from this one, and both rules give the same outcome for the CARE case. The v3 spec has no permission or licence criterion.
